idiom_name: structural object type with only the consumed members + destructuring defaults (zod z.object() strips unknown keys by default)
implementation_notes: TypeScript's object types are structural and open: a value carrying extra properties is still assignable to the interface you declare, and excess-property checking only fires on fresh object literals, so declaring just the members you consume is the type-level half of the pattern - no binding layer needs to be configured because none is implied. At runtime nothing is validated (the types are erased), so the reader is a narrow function that destructures with defaults from an `unknown`/Partial-typed payload, or a parser schema such as zod, whose z.object() strips unrecognised keys by default while .passthrough() keeps them and .strict() rejects them - the deliberate choice between tolerant, preserving and strict reading.
pitfalls: Types are erased, so `payload as OrderPayload` asserts rather than checks: a renamed key binds undefined and the default silently takes over - parse to `unknown` and validate (zod/io-ts) at the boundary if drift must be detected.

Excess-property checks apply only to fresh object literals; assigning through an intermediate variable or an index signature lets arbitrary extra properties through, so they are not runtime validation.

Optional members plus `strictNullChecks` mean every consumed field may be undefined at the type level; defaults must be applied deliberately (destructuring, ??, schema .default()), otherwise undefined flows inward and fails later.
